title: Staying Human in an AI World
description: Finding room for curiosity, connection, and a life of our own as the world keeps getting smarter.
body: Lately, I’ve been thinking about what it means to build a life in a world that keeps getting smarter.

AI can write, create, explain, and help us do things that once felt out of reach. It’s exciting. It’s also a little unsettling. When so much can happen in seconds, it’s easy to feel like we should always be doing more.
I’m learning to ask a different question: what do I actually want to make time for?

Maybe using AI well means spending less time staring at a blank page and more time deciding what I want to say. Getting help with a difficult task, then closing the laptop to have dinner with someone I love. Staying curious without feeling obliged to keep up with every new tool.
I don’t have a grand answer yet. This blog is a place to think through those questions as they come.
For now, I’m happy to have a little help getting started—and a reason to keep thinking for myself.

title: The art of paying attention
description: A quieter kind of ambition: noticing the small things that make a life feel like your own.
body: There is a particular kind of clarity that arrives when you stop trying to fill every quiet moment. A walk without headphones. A cup of coffee before the first notification. A conversation with room for a pause.
Attention is a practice. It asks us to look again at the things we have learned to overlook, and to find something worth keeping in an ordinary day.

title: Make room for the unfinished
description: On starting before you feel ready, and letting the work teach you what comes next.
body: A blank page can feel like an invitation or a test. Sometimes the only difference is whether we give ourselves permission to begin badly.
Not every idea needs to become something immediately. Some need a notebook, a little patience, and a return visit.

title: A place to think out loud
description: Why keep a little corner of the internet? Because some thoughts deserve more than a passing moment.
body: A personal website is a place to gather the things that stay with you. Ideas, questions, reading notes, and stories that have not quite found a home anywhere else.
The pleasure is in building it slowly. One observation becomes a paragraph; a paragraph becomes a conversation.
